questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To nip in the bud'
o: To stop something at an early stage
questions.x: 'To nip in the bud' means: to stop something at an early stage.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To smell a rat'
questions.x: 'To smell a rat' means: to suspect something is wrong.

Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Scarcely had the auditors arrived / when the accountant / presented the ledgers.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. The sentence is correct: 'Scarcely…when' is the right pair.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Laconic'.
questions.x: 'Laconic' means concise. 'Verbose' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To sit on the fence' mean?
questions.x: 'To sit on the fence' means: to avoid taking sides.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: OSTENTATIOUS
questions.x: 'Ostentatious' means showy. 'Modest' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Quiescent'.
questions.x: 'Quiescent' is the opposite of 'Active'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Quiescent'.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: TACTFUL
questions.x: 'Tactful' is the opposite of 'Blunt'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Tactful'.

questions.q: The auditor insisted ____ seeing the original vouchers.
questions.x: 'Insist on' + gerund.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A detailed plan of a journey'
questions.x: 'Itinerary' means a detailed plan of a journey.

questions.q: What example does the author use to show that automation can change rather than eliminate jobs?
questions.x: Answer: 'ATMs in banks'. The ATM example shows tellers' roles shifting to advisory work. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Automation does not simply destroy jobs; it changes their content. When banks installed ATMs, many expected tellers to vanish. Instead, branches became cheaper to run, banks opened more of them, and tellers shifted towards advising customers. The lesson is not that technology is always kind to workers, but that outcomes depend on how firms and governments respond. Retraining, portable benefits and support during transitions decide whether a new machine becomes a threat or an opportunity.

questions.q: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
o: Public policy influences whether automation helps or harms workers
questions.x: Answer: 'Public policy influences whether automation helps or harms workers'. The author says outcomes 'depend on how firms and governments respond'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Automation does not simply destroy jobs; it changes their content. When banks installed ATMs, many expected tellers to vanish. The lesson is not that technology is always kind to workers, but that outcomes depend on how firms and governments respond. Retraining, portable benefits and support during transitions decide whether a new machine becomes a threat or an opportunity.

questions.q: Who was the leader of the Ghadar movement and its newspaper 'Ghadar'?
questions.x: The party included Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha and others.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Vernacular Press Act and the Delhi Durbar of 1877?
questions.x: Lord Lytton was Viceroy during the Vernacular Press Act and the Delhi Durbar of 1877.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Formation of Muslim League 2. Ghadar Party 3. Home Rule League 4. Swaraj Party
questions.x: Muslim League (1906), Ghadar Party (1913), Home Rule League (1916), Swaraj Party (1923).

questions.q: The book 'Neel Darpan' was written by:
questions.x: 'Neel Darpan' was written by Dinabandhu Mitra.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. INA trials 2. RIN mutiny 3. Shimla Conference 4. Direct Action Day
questions.x: Shimla Conference (June 1945), INA trials (from Nov 1945), RIN mutiny (Feb 1946), Direct Action Day (Aug 1946).

questions.q: Jatin Das died in Lahore jail in 1929 after a hunger strike lasting:
questions.x: Correct answer: 63 days. He demanded better treatment of political prisoners.

questions.q: Who among the following led the 'Vaikom Satyagraha' in Kerala?
o: T. K. Madhavan and K. Kelappan, with support from Periyar
questions.x: Correct answer: T. K. Madhavan and K. Kelappan, with support from Periyar. It demanded access for lower castes to roads near the Vaikom temple.

questions.q: The 'Ahom revolt' (1828) took place in:
questions.x: Ahom nobles resisted British annexation after the First Anglo-Burmese War.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The 'August Offer' (1940) was rejected by the Congress.
Reason (R): It promised a Constituent Assembly immediately with full powers.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is true; R is false — it promised a constitution-making body only after the war and an expanded Executive Council.

questions.q: The 1896 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Rahimtulla M. Sayani, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Calcutta; it was the session at which 'Vande Mataram' was first sung (by Tagore).

questions.q: World Tourism Day is observed on:
questions.x: World Tourism Day: 27 September.

questions.q: The headquarters of the OECD is located in:
questions.x: OECD: headquartered in Paris.

questions.q: Friedrich Merz became the Chancellor of which country in May 2025?
questions.x: Correct answer: Germany. He leads the Christian Democratic Union.

questions.q: India's proposed space station is named:
questions.x: Correct answer: Bharatiya Antariksh Station. The first module is targeted for 2028 and full station by 2035.

questions.q: The 'Good Governance Index' is published by:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
questions.x: 'Good Governance Index' is brought out by Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Ajeya Warrior' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Ajeya Warrior' is a bilateral exercise between India and United Kingdom.

questions.q: The 'Voice of the Global South' summits were convened by:
questions.x: India hosted the first two in 2023 to bring developing countries' priorities to the G20.

questions.q: BharatNet aims to provide:
o: Broadband connectivity to all gram panchayats
questions.x: Correct answer: Broadband connectivity to all gram panchayats. It is one of the largest rural telecom projects.

questions.q: The 'Green Credit Programme' notified in 2023 aims to:
o: Incentivise voluntary environmental actions such as tree plantation through tradable credits
questions.x: It is administered by the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education.

questions.q: The 2028 Summer Olympics, which will include cricket, will be held in:
questions.x: Correct answer: Los Angeles. Brisbane will host in 2032.

questions.q: In the GST Council, the Centre's vote carries what weight of the total votes cast?
questions.x: States together have two-thirds; decisions need a three-fourths majority.

questions.q: In April 2025, in State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu, the Supreme Court addressed which issue?
o: Delays by the Governor in granting assent to bills, laying down timelines
questions.x: The Court held that Governors cannot indefinitely withhold action on bills and set timelines; the issue was later referred to a Presidential reference (Article 143).

questions.q: Article 26 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Early childhood care and education for children below six years
Promotion of international peace and security
questions.x: Article 26: Freedom to manage religious affairs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Directive Principles:
1. They are enforceable by courts.
2. They are fundamental in the governance of the country.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is incorrect; Statement 2 is correct.
Article 37 makes them non-justiciable but fundamental in governance.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment reorganised States on a linguistic basis and abolished Part A, B, C, D classification?
questions.x: It was the 7th Amendment Act of 1956.

questions.q: Under the 73rd Amendment, elections to Panchayats are conducted by the:
questions.x: Correct answer: State Election Commission. Article 243K.

questions.q: Article 131 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Procedure for impeachment of the President
Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States
Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.x: Article 131: Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Article 114 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States
Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights
questions.x: Article 114: Appropriation Bills.

questions.q: The idea of 'Fundamental Duties' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of:
questions.x: Fundamental Duties were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, inspired by the Soviet Constitution.

questions.q:
Consider the following bodies:
1. Election Commission of India
2. NITI Aayog
3. Finance Commission
4. National Human Rights Commission
How many of the above are constitutional bodies?
questions.x:
2 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Only the Election Commission and the Finance Commission are constitutional bodies.

questions.q: 'Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organisations' scheme (2020) aims to:
o: Help small farmers aggregate for better bargaining, inputs and market access
questions.x: Correct answer: Help small farmers aggregate for better bargaining, inputs and market access. FPOs are registered as companies or cooperatives.

questions.q: India has committed to achieve net-zero emissions by:
questions.x: Correct answer: 2070. Announced at COP26 in 2021.

questions.q: 'Opportunity cost' refers to:
o: The value of the next best alternative forgone
questions.x: Correct answer: The value of the next best alternative forgone. It is central to economic decision making.

questions.q: Tuhin Kanta Pandey became the Chairman of SEBI in March 2025, succeeding:
questions.x: Madhabi Puri Buch was the first woman SEBI chief.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Regional Rural Banks:
1. They are sponsored by commercial banks.
2. They focus on credit to small farmers, artisans and rural poor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
Both statements are correct.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 20% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹1700 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.2 = 5.
Total deposits = 1700 × 5 = ₹8,500 crore (of which new credit = ₹6,800 crore).

questions.q: The 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme (2023) supports:
o: Traditional artisans and craftspeople with skilling, toolkits and collateral-free credit
questions.x: Correct answer: Traditional artisans and craftspeople with skilling, toolkits and collateral-free credit. It covers 18 traditional trades.

questions.q: A 'Laffer curve' suggests that beyond a point, raising tax rates:
questions.x: Correct answer: Reduces tax revenue. High rates discourage economic activity and encourage evasion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fiscal deficit includes interest payments.
2. Primary deficit is always larger than fiscal deficit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments, so it is smaller when interest is positive.

questions.q: The Phillips curve depicts an inverse relationship between:
questions.x: Correct answer: Inflation and unemployment. The Laffer curve relates tax rates and revenue.

questions.q: Activity-Based Costing allocates overheads on the basis of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Cost drivers of activities. ABC improves accuracy in multi-product firms.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹35,000, Debtors ₹45,000, Inventory ₹50,000, Prepaid expenses ₹7,500, Creditors ₹75,000, Bills payable ₹5,000 and Outstanding expenses ₹7,500. Its current ratio is:
Price–Earnings (P/E) ratio equals:
o: Market price per share ÷ Earnings per share
questions.x: Correct answer: Market price per share ÷ Earnings per share. P/E reflects how much investors pay per rupee of earnings.

questions.q: If the trial balance does not agree, the difference is temporarily placed in:
questions.x: The suspense account is closed when errors are located and rectified.

questions.q: The current ratio of a company is 1.75 : 1 and its working capital is ₹41,250. Its current assets amount to:
questions.x:
Let current liabilities = x. Then current assets = 1.75x and working capital = 1.75x − x = 0.75x.
0.75x = 41,250 → x = ₹55,000.
Current assets = 1.75 × 55,000 = ₹96,250.

questions.q: Days of grace allowed on a time bill of exchange in India are:
questions.x: Under the Negotiable Instruments Act, three days of grace are added to compute the due date (not for bills payable on demand).

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹1,000 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 8% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 1,000 = ₹12,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 12,000 × 8% × 6/12 = ₹480.

questions.q: The profits of a firm for the last 4 years were ₹82,000, ₹39,000, ₹20,000, ₹47,000. Goodwill is to be valued at 2 years' purchase of the average profit. Goodwill is:
The National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) was constituted under the:
questions.x: NFRA oversees audit quality and recommends accounting and auditing standards.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹60,000; Purchases ₹3,15,000; Purchase returns ₹1,000; Carriage inwards ₹1,000; Sales ₹3,92,500; Sales returns ₹3,000; Closing stock ₹50,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 60,000 + 3,15,000 − 1,000 + 1,000 − 50,000 = ₹3,25,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 3,92,500 − 3,000 − 3,25,000 = ₹64,500.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹60,000, closing inventory is ₹65,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹6,25,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (60,000 + 65,000) / 2 = ₹62,500.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 6,25,000 / 62,500 = 10 times.

questions.q: Under the modern (American) approach, an increase in an asset is recorded by a:
questions.x: Assets and expenses increase with debits; liabilities, capital and incomes increase with credits.

questions.q: Under Ind AS, a 'complete set of financial statements' includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.x: The directors' report is required under the Companies Act but is not part of financial statements.

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 5 : 2. They admit R for a 1/5 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
Under the OSH Code, if a contravention of safety provisions causes the death of a worker, a court may direct that a portion of the fine be paid to:
o: The victim or the legal heirs
questions.x: Courts may direct that not less than 50% of the fine be paid as compensation to the victim or legal heirs.

questions.q: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 was enacted largely on the recommendation of:
o: The Royal Commission on Labour (Whitley Commission)
questions.x: The Whitley Commission (1931) found arbitrary deductions and delays, leading to the 1936 Act.

questions.q: Which case held that temporary employees performing the same duties as regular employees are entitled to the minimum of the pay scale of regular employees ('equal pay for equal work')?
o: Secretary, State of Karnataka v. Umadevi (2006)
State of Punjab v. Jagjit Singh (2016)
Steel Authority of India v. National Union Waterfront Workers (2001)
questions.x: In Jagjit Singh (2016), the Court extended equal pay for equal work to temporary/contractual employees.

questions.q: If no trade union in an establishment has 51% membership, the IR Code provides for a negotiating council comprising unions that have at least what membership?
questions.x: A negotiating council is formed with representatives of unions having not less than 20% of the workers as members.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Under the IR Code, a fixed-term employee is entitled to the same wages as a permanent employee doing similar work.
Reason (R): Fixed-term employees are entitled to gratuity only after five years of continuous service.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is correct. R is false — fixed-term employees qualify for pro-rata gratuity after one year.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of Labour Code and the number of laws it subsumes:
1. Code on Wages, 2019 — 4 laws
2. Industrial Relations Code, 2020 — 3 laws
3. Code on Social Security, 2020 — 13 laws
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Code on Wages subsumes 4 laws and the IR Code 3. The Code on Social Security subsumes 9 laws; it is the OSH Code that subsumes 13.

questions.q: Labour turnover rate by the 'separation method' is:
o: Number of separations during the period ÷ average number of workers × 100
questions.x: Separation method uses exits; replacement and flux methods use replacements and (separations + accessions).

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, the 'accounting year' for bonus purposes ordinarily means:
o: The year ending on the date of the last wage revision
The year commencing on 1 April, unless the establishment's books close on another date
Any 12 months chosen by the union
questions.x: Accounting year generally means the year beginning 1 April; for companies, the period for which accounts are prepared.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, a retrenched worker must be given preference when the employer proposes to re-employ persons within:
questions.x: Section 72: retrenched workers get preference for re-employment if the employer recruits within one year.

questions.q: The 'residual claimant theory' of wages, which says workers get what remains after rent, interest and profit are paid, was proposed by:
questions.x: Walker's theory treats labour as the residual claimant to the product.

questions.q: The 'hot stove rule' of discipline, attributed to Douglas McGregor, emphasises that discipline should be:
o: Immediate, consistent, impersonal and with prior warning
questions.x: Like touching a hot stove: the burn is immediate, consistent, impersonal and preceded by warning (the stove looks hot).

questions.q: The 'Giri Approach' in Indian industrial relations, associated with V. V. Giri, favoured:
o: Collective bargaining and bipartite settlement over compulsory adjudication
questions.x: As Labour Minister (1952–54) V. V. Giri advocated voluntary negotiation and bipartism rather than state intervention.

questions.q: In which year was the Plantations Labour Act enacted?
questions.x: The Plantations Labour Act was enacted in 1951.

questions.q: A woman employee with two surviving children expects her third child. Her maternity benefit entitlement is:
o: 12 weeks, of which not more than 6 weeks can precede delivery
questions.x: For a woman with two or more surviving children the benefit is 12 weeks (up to 6 weeks before delivery).

questions.q: The Declaration of Philadelphia (1944), annexed to the ILO Constitution, proclaimed that:
o: Trade unions must register with the ILO
Minimum wages should be uniform worldwide
questions.x: It restated the ILO's aims and proclaimed 'labour is not a commodity' and 'poverty anywhere constitutes a danger to prosperity everywhere'.

questions.q: The current base year of the CPI-IW series released by the Labour Bureau is:
questions.x: The CPI-IW base was revised from 2001 to 2016 = 100 in 2020.

questions.q: PM-JAY was launched in September 2018 at:
questions.x: The scheme was launched on 23 September 2018 at Ranchi, Jharkhand.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 26 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹380. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 26-week period including Sundays: 26 × 7 = 182 days.
Amount = ₹380 × 182 = ₹69,160. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹59,280.)

questions.q: Damages under Section 14B for delayed EPF remittance (EPF Scheme) rise with the period of default. For a delay of more than six months, the rate is:
questions.x: Rates (since 2016): up to 2 months — 5%, 2–4 months — 10%, 4–6 months — 15%, above 6 months — 25% per annum.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of a fully funded pension system?
o: It is less exposed to demographic ageing
questions.x: Financing current pensioners from current contributions is the PAYG principle.

questions.q: An employee whose average daily wage is ₹152 works in an ESI-covered factory and earns ₹16,500 in a month. Which statement about the month's contribution is correct?
o: Neither pays, as low-wage employees are excluded from coverage
Only the employer pays 3.25% (≈ ₹537); the employee's share is exempt
questions.x: Employees whose average daily wage is up to ₹176 are exempt from paying their own 0.75% share, but they remain covered and the employer must still pay 3.25% of wages. Here employer share ≈ ₹537.

questions.q: Orphan pension under EPS 1995 is payable at what share of the widow pension?
questions.x: Orphan pension is 75% of the widow pension, for two orphans at a time till 25.

questions.q: Contributions under the EPF & MP Act are calculated on 'basic wages', DA, retaining allowance and:
o: Cash value of any food concession
questions.x: Section 6 includes cash value of food concession; HRA, overtime, bonus and commission are excluded from basic wages.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Code on Social Security permits EPF coverage of establishments with fewer than 20 employees on a voluntary basis.
Reason (R): The Code makes EPF mandatory for all establishments irrespective of size.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is true; R is false — mandatory coverage is for 20 or more employees.

questions.q: The Seamen's Provident Fund for seafarers is administered separately under the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Seamen's Provident Fund Act, 1966. Seafarers have a separate PF organisation (SPFO) in Mumbai.

questions.q: On normal exit from NPS at 60, a subscriber must use at least what portion of the corpus to buy an annuity (under the rules applicable to government subscribers)?
questions.x: At least 40% must be annuitised; up to 60% may be withdrawn as a lump sum (tax-free).

questions.q: A seasonal establishment employee worked for 12 seasons with last drawn wages of ₹26,000 per month. Gratuity at 7 days per season is:
Which organisation provides super-specialty treatment to ESI beneficiaries through tie-ups and its own hospitals?
questions.x: ESIC provides super-specialty care through its hospitals and tie-up hospitals; convergence with PM-JAY has also been announced.

questions.q: The causative agent of ringworm is:
o: Wuchereria bancrofti (nematode worm, spread by Culex mosquitoes)
questions.x: Ringworm: Dermatophyte fungi such as Trichophyton.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure speed of rotation (rpm)?
questions.x: Tachometer measures speed of rotation (rpm).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ozone layer:
1. It is found mainly in the stratosphere.
2. Chlorofluorocarbons deplete it.
3. It absorbs most of the Sun's infrared radiation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation, not most infrared.

questions.q: A 'large language model' (LLM) is:
o: An AI model trained on vast text data to understand and generate language
questions.x: Correct answer: An AI model trained on vast text data to understand and generate language. Generative AI chatbots are built on LLMs.

questions.q: Which is the correct ascending order of memory units?
questions.x: Correct answer: KB < MB < GB < TB < PB. Each step is 1,024 times the previous.

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'Graphics Processing Unit'?
questions.x: Graphics Processing Unit is abbreviated as GPU.

questions.q: The 'Weber' is the SI unit of:
questions.x: Weber measures magnetic flux.

questions.q: Vaccines work by:
o: Killing all bacteria in the body
Stimulating the immune system to produce memory against a pathogen
questions.x: Correct answer: Stimulating the immune system to produce memory against a pathogen. They contain weakened/inactivated pathogens or their components.

questions.q: 'Biodiversity hotspots' in India include:
o: The Himalaya, Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Sundaland (Nicobar)
questions.x: Correct answer: The Himalaya, Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Sundaland (Nicobar). India has parts of four of the world's 36 hotspots.

questions.q: HCl (hydrochloric acid) is commonly known as:
questions.x: HCl (hydrochloric acid) is muriatic acid.

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on the Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.x: Correct answer: 9.8 m/s². On the Moon it is about one-sixth, about 1.6 m/s².

questions.q: The Information Technology Act was enacted in:
questions.x: Correct answer: 2000. It was amended significantly in 2008.

questions.q:
New establishments registered — 2020: 100  |  2021: 85  |  2022: 110  |  2023: 100  |  2024: 140.
What is the percentage change from 2020 to 2022?
questions.x:
Change = 110 − 100 = 10 on a base of 100 (earlier year).
% change = 10/100 × 100 = 10% → 10% increase.

questions.q: A vessel holds 20 litres of pure milk. 2 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 20 × (1 − 2/20)² = 20 × (0.9)² = 16.2 litres.
Removing 2 × 2 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.

questions.q: ₹19,000 is invested for 1 year at 10% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 10/2 = 5%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 19,000 × (1 + 5/100)² = ₹20,947.50.
CI = ₹1,947.50 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹1,900).

questions.q: How many arrangements of the letters of 'VOUCHER' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 5,040 (all letters are distinct).
Vowels together = 120 × 6 = 720.
Not all together = 5,040 − 720 = 4,320.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 8, 38, 15, 36, 22, 34, 29, ?
questions.x: Two interleaved series: odd positions 8, 15, 22, 29 (+7); even positions 38, 36, 34 (−2). The 8th term belongs to the even series: 34 − 2 = 32.

questions.q: Find the unit digit of 19^26 + 72^90.
questions.x:
Only last digits matter.
Unit digit of first term (base ending 9, cycle 9,1,9,1; 26 → position 2) = 1.
Unit digit of second term (base ending 2, cycle 2,4,8,6; 90 → position 2) = 4.
1 + 4 → unit digit 5.

questions.q: The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 6 : 5 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 4 : 3. If each of them saves ₹10,000 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 6k, 5k and expenditures = 4m, 3m.
6k − 4m = 5k − 3m = 10,000 → 1k = 1m.
Solving gives k = 5,000, m = 5,000.
P's income = 6 × 5,000 = ₹30,000 (check: ₹30,000 − ₹20,000 = ₹10,000).

questions.q: A field officer starts from point O and walks 3 km towards North, then turns right and walks 11 km, then turns left and walks 9 km, and finally turns left and walks 16 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: +3 +9 = 12 km → 12 km North.
East–West: +11 -16 = -5 km → 5 km West.
Distance = √(5² + 12²) = 13 km, towards North-West.

questions.q: In a certain code language, HEALTH is written as IDBKUG. How is DEBIT written in that code?
questions.x:
Compare HEALTH → IDBKUG: H→I, E→D, A→B…
Rule: letters in odd positions move 1 forward and letters in even positions move 1 backward.
Applying it to DEBIT gives EDCHU.

questions.q: Find the remainder when 3^70 is divided by 13.
questions.x:
Powers of 3 mod 13: 3, 9, 1 → cycle length 3.
70 = 3 × 23 + 1 → 3^70 ≡ 3^1 ≡ 3 (mod 13).

questions.q: In a row, Sonal is 16th from the left and Asif is 19th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Sonal becomes 23rd from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Sonal occupies Asif's old place, which is 19th from the right and now 23rd from the left.
Total = 23 + 19 − 1 = 41.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a cistern in 6 hours and 18 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 45 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(6, 18, 45) = 90 units.
Rates: +15, +5, −2 units/hour → net 18 units/hour.
Time = 90 / 18 = 5 hours.

questions.q: Two trains of lengths 210 m and 300 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 36 km/h and 54 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.x:
Opposite directions → relative speed = 36 + 54 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s.
Distance = sum of lengths = 510 m.
Time = 510 / 25 = 20.4 s.

questions.q: a clerk can paint a hall in 20 days and an assistant in 60 days. They start together, but a clerk leaves after 6 days. In how many days in all is the work completed?
questions.x:
Work done together in 6 days = 6 × (1/20 + 1/60) = 6/15 = 2/5.
Remaining = 3/5, done by an assistant alone in 3/5 × 60 = 36 days.
Total = 6 + 36 = 42 days.
